lead.headline: Jensen Huang resigns from Nvidia; Anthropic sets its IPO price range
lead.dek: Colette Kress becomes interim chief executive as Congress and an outside law firm look into the founder's exit, while Anthropic's roadshow names 825 million shares at $70 to $78.

bottom_line: Nvidia's board announced that Jensen Huang has resigned as chief executive, president and director, with chief financial officer Colette Kress serving as interim chief executive. Huang has agreed to testify to House committees, and Democrats opened a separate inquiry into export licences for chips sold to China. Anthropic's roadshow filing sets 825 million shares at $70 to $78 under the symbol ANT, and Thinking Machines released open weights for a 594 billion parameter model.

numbers.label: Class A shares in Anthropic's proposed offering, 801 million from the company, per its roadshow notice
Planned 2027 spending by Nebius, stated on its third-quarter earnings call
Public Claude Code settings files, of over 100,000 found, that held secrets, per Apiiro

front.summary: The lab board is dominated by corporate events: an Nvidia leadership change and Anthropic's public offering terms. On the product side, Thinking Machines released open weights, Anthropic previewed self-hosted agents and Meta's Muse agent gained phone calling. Most performance numbers come from the makers or from one newsletter's roundup.

axes.name: Anthropic
axes.text: Anthropic launched its roadshow, offering 825 million Class A shares at an expected $70 to $78 each, and applied to list on Nasdaq as ANT. A newsletter roundup also reports a private beta of self-hosted Claude Managed Agents and a beta of Claude Meetings.

axes.name: Google DeepMind
axes.text: DeepMind unveiled Gemini Robotics 2.5 and an open safety benchmark called ASIMOV-jailbreak. Google says success rates rose 30 to 100 percent over the prior version, and Artificial Analysis rated its new Gemini 4 Hydrogen model strong on hallucination but weaker on terminal tasks.

axes.name: OpenAI
axes.text: A newsletter roundup says OpenAI launched two cyber products, Daybreak Defense Factory and Daybreak Red Team. At a developer summit, two OpenAI engineers described Codex cloud environments, voice control and personal agents.

axes.name: Meta
axes.text: Meta's consumer agent Muse can now place phone calls to US businesses for paid subscribers, announced by Alexandr Wang. TechCrunch notes Muse passed 10 million users last month, per the company.

axes.name: Thinking Machines
axes.text: The company released Inkling 2 Small under an Apache 2.0 licence. A newsletter describes it as a mixture-of-experts model with 594 billion total and 17 billion active parameters, and reports leaderboard results from Arena.

axes.name: Nvidia
axes.text: Nvidia's board announced that Jensen Huang resigned as chief executive, president and director after reports of affairs, including one with a woman accused of being a Chinese spy. Chief financial officer Colette Kress is interim chief executive, and the company reports earnings on Tuesday.

axes.name: Compute and policy
axes.text: Huang agreed to testify to House committees, and two Democrats opened an inquiry into Commerce Department chip licences. Separately, Nebius outlined $40 billion of 2027 spending, financed by customer prepayments and contract-backed loans.

sections.summary: Open weights and independent tests were the model news. Thinking Machines released a large open model, and outside testers gave a mixed picture of Google's Gemini 4 Hydrogen.

items.headline: Thinking Machines releases Inkling 2 Small as open weights
items.summary: The weights come under an Apache 2.0 licence, according to a Latent Space roundup that cites the company. The model is a mixture-of-experts design with 594 billion total and 17 billion active parameters, text and image input, and up to 1 million tokens of context. The roundup reports it as the top US open model on the Code Arena WebDev leaderboard.

items.headline: Independent tests give Gemini 4 Hydrogen mixed marks
items.summary: Artificial Analysis scored Hydrogen at 54 on its index at the highest thinking level, one point behind two rival models, and reported an 8 percent hallucination rate. It scored 54 percent on Terminal-Bench 4.0, below the 64 percent it reported for Claude Sonnet 5.5. Testers also reported runaway reasoning on some prompts.

items.headline: Perplexity adds span-locating to its open Decider models
items.summary: Perplexity released Decider v1.3 as open weights, adding a locate function that returns span positions for tasks such as entity recognition and personal-data detection. Perplexity says it is 6.54 points more accurate than its production classifiers across 63 tasks. The models are free on OpenRouter for one week, the roundup says.

sections.summary: Research items this edition come with caveats attached. A robotics result is a lab figure, a chip-tracing claim is disputed, and a new engineering benchmark was built by a company that sells to labs.

items.headline: From November 10: DeepMind says Gemini Robotics 2.5 handles finer tasks
items.summary: Google DeepMind reports a 30 to 100 percent higher success rate than the prior version, tested on more than 200 activities. Humanoid robots using it kitted car parts in European Mercedes-Benz factories with a 96 percent success rate, and a DeepMind director called closing the last 4 percent a steep road. DeepMind also released an open safety benchmark, ASIMOV-jailbreak.

items.headline: Researcher says weight patterns show Chinese models trained on Blackwell chips
items.summary: Will Depue reports that initialization patterns in released weights identify the GPU type used, and says six Chinese models, including DeepSeek-V4-Pro and Kimi K3, started on Blackwell systems. Critics quoted in the roundup say the scale is small against China's installed compute and that the use was already known. Depue's work is not independently confirmed on the record.

items.headline: Mercor benchmark ranks models on long engineering projects
items.summary: Mercor's OWE-Bench has 26 long-horizon engineering projects. Mercor reports Fable 5.2 at 54.6 percent, GPT-6 Astra at 44.2 percent and Opus 5.5 at 41.6 percent. The roundup notes more than 200 million tokens per problem, and the scores are the benchmark owner's own.

sections.summary: Agent products moved toward self-hosting and phone calls, while a security researcher showed an AI app builder exposing thousands of shared projects. The pattern is more autonomy shipped alongside more questions about access and sharing.

items.headline: Anthropic previews self-hosted Claude Managed Agents
items.summary: A private beta lets customers run the agent harness, sandboxes and session history in their own cloud or on their own servers, and choose where Claude requests go, according to the ClaudeDevs account cited by Latent Space. The roundup says it adds agent identity, telemetry, kill switches and an evaluation product.

items.headline: Claude Meetings enters beta for Team and Enterprise plans
items.summary: The feature lets Claude join video calls and build documents and whiteboards in real time, according to the Claude account as cited by Latent Space. The roundup ranks the announcement as the most-engaged post of the day, at 59.3 thousand.

items.headline: Meta's Muse agent can phone US businesses for paying users
items.summary: Alexandr Wang, Meta's chief AI officer, announced the feature on November 12 after a September test. Plans start at $20 a month. TechCrunch notes some businesses hang up when they detect an AI caller.

items.headline: From November 10: Grok Build share links expose thousands of projects
items.summary: Security firm Claroc says the share links of the coding agent from SpaceXSI can be enumerated, exposing business data from thousands of apps, including 24 built by SpaceXSI itself. Ars Technica reports the company began removing its own links within hours of being asked questions.

sections.summary: Nvidia's leadership change dominates, with Congress and Democrats both opening lines of inquiry. Elsewhere, Anthropic put numbers on its offering, Nebius laid out a large spending plan and the FAA widened an AI scheduling tool.

items.headline: Nvidia names Colette Kress interim chief after Huang resigns
items.summary: Nvidia's board said Huang left as president, chief executive and director effective immediately. Kress, chief financial officer since 2013, keeps that job while leading the company. Latent Space reports the board has opened a search and named Harvey Jones its first chair.

items.headline: Huang agrees to testify to House committees by Thanksgiving
items.summary: House Foreign Affairs chairman Brian Mast said Huang agreed on Wednesday to appear after lawmakers threatened a subpoena, according to Bloomberg and NBC News. The session will be closed to the public but recorded and transcribed.

items.headline: Neal and Wyden open an inquiry into how chip licences were handled
items.summary: The two Democrats asked Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to preserve records on the arrangement under which H200 chips were routed through the United States and taxed before export to China. They allege the arrangement is illegal; as minority members they cannot compel answers.

items.headline: From November 10: Anthropic offers 825 million shares in its IPO
items.summary: Anthropic said 801,351,354 shares come from the company and 23,648,646 from existing stockholders at an expected $70 to $78 each. It applied to list on Nasdaq as ANT, and underwriters hold an option on 123,750,000 more shares.

items.headline: Nebius plans $40 billion of 2027 spending as site delays persist
items.summary: The neocloud company said on its earnings call it will fund the buildout with customer prepayments and loans backed by contracts. Only about half of the Microsoft capacity at its Vineland, New Jersey site is due this year, and its chief executive said delays affect the industry.

items.headline: FAA extends its SMART scheduling tool to every air traffic centre
items.summary: The FAA says the $875 million system rerouted 180 flights in Washington airspace since September 21, saving about 10 minutes per flight, and will now cover all 22 centres. These are the agency's figures. The controllers' union says it was not involved in the design or testing.

explainer.title: What a mixture-of-experts model is, and what 'active parameters' means
explainer.text:
A mixture-of-experts model is built from several expert networks plus a gating function. For each input, the gate produces weights that decide how much each expert contributes, and the outputs are combined into one answer. Wikipedia describes the idea as dividing a problem into regions, with different experts covering different regions.

This is why model announcements often quote two sizes. A newsletter describes Thinking Machines' Inkling 2 Small as 594 billion total and 17 billion active parameters. Total counts every expert; active counts the part used at a time. When you compare models, check which of the two figures a company is quoting before drawing conclusions from the headline number.

playbook.title: Quiz yourself on the agent's patch before you accept it
playbook.who: Mihail Eric, who teaches The Modern Software Developer at Stanford and leads AI at Monaco
playbook.summary: Eric argues that understanding the change is now the bottleneck, since an agent can write a feature in an afternoon. He points to Geoffrey Litt's explain-diff skill, which turns a change into a visual walkthrough and then quizzes you on it. Use it on any patch your agent just produced.
steps: Run an explain-diff style skill on the change the agent just wrote, to get a walkthrough of what changed.
Answer the quiz questions without looking at the code, and note which question makes you reopen it.
Spend your review time on the parts you could not answer from the walkthrough.
Give background agents a workspace where they can run the product, reproduce a failure and test their patch before you review.

playbook.title: Use voice as a control plane for your coding agents
playbook.who: Dominik Kundel and Charlie Guo, Developer Experience engineers at OpenAI
playbook.summary: At the AI Engineer Code Summit, the two described using voice for more than dictation. Guo treats it as a way to manage the whole set of agent threads, and Kundel hands local work to the cloud and starts tasks from a personal agent before he reaches his desk.
steps: Use voice to check in on running threads, start new ones and pull data from other apps, not only to dictate prompts.
Ask your local Codex to hand a task to a cloud environment when you want it to keep running without your laptop.
Turn the effort level down when a task does not need heavy reasoning.
Ask the agents themselves for help with the tool, and do not get attached to your current way of working.

playbook.title: Keep Claude Code's local settings file out of git and use auto mode
playbook.who: Boris Cherny, Claude Code at Anthropic, quoted by Ars Technica
playbook.summary: Researchers at Apiiro found over 100,000 public repositories containing the file where Claude Code stores approved shell commands, and about 1,100 held secrets. Cherny's advice, given in a Hacker News thread, is to avoid checking the file in and to let auto mode handle routine permission prompts.
steps: Do not commit the local settings file, which Cherny says should pretty much never be checked in.
Use auto mode, which routes routine permission prompts through classifiers, instead of hand-maintaining allow and deny lists.
Run a secret scanner over your repositories, remembering Apiiro found 215 secrets that two popular scanners missed.

playbook.title: From October: Name the library, then tell the model to make it more fun
playbook.who: Simon Willison, developer and author of Simon Willison's Weblog
playbook.summary: Included from October 28 because it is the clearest recent write-up of prompts that produced playable browser games. Willison says telling models to use three.js works well, and that a follow-up asking for much more fun improved his results.
steps: Name the technology you want, such as three.js, in the first prompt.
State the quality bar in the prompt, for example asking the model to think hard about making the result both fun and beautiful.
After a working first build, send a plain follow-up such as asking it to make the result a lot more fun.

audio.script:
This is The A I Dispatch for Friday, November thirteenth, twenty twenty six. The bottom line. Nvidia announced that Jensen Huang has resigned as chief executive, president and board member, and chief financial officer Colette Kress is interim chief executive. Congress and two Democrats have opened separate lines of inquiry, and Anthropic's roadshow names its share count and price range.

Start with the models. Thinking Machines released Inkling 2 Small as open weights under an Apache two point oh licence. A Latent Space roundup describes it as a mixture of experts model with five hundred ninety four billion total parameters and seventeen billion active. The same roundup reports that it ranks as the top American open model on the Code Arena web development leaderboard. That is a leaderboard result relayed by one newsletter, so treat it as a claim.

Independent testing of Google's Gemini 4 Hydrogen gave a mixed picture. Artificial Analysis scored it fifty four at the highest thinking level, one point behind two rivals, with an eight percent hallucination rate. On Terminal Bench four point oh it scored fifty four percent, below the sixty four percent reported for Claude Sonnet five point five. Some testers also saw runaway reasoning on certain prompts. Perplexity also released open Decider models that can now return the positions of spans in text. Perplexity says they are six point five four points more accurate than its production classifiers across sixty three tasks.

Now research. From November tenth, Google DeepMind says Gemini Robotics two point five has a thirty to one hundred percent higher success rate than the last version. In European Mercedes Benz factories, humanoid robots using it kitted car parts with a ninety six percent success rate. A DeepMind director called closing the last four percent a steep road. Separately, researcher Will Depue says patterns in released model weights show six Chinese models started training on Blackwell chips. Critics say the scale is small and the use was already known. And Mercor, which owns a new engineering benchmark, reports that Fable five point two scored fifty four point six percent, ahead of two rival models. Those scores come from the benchmark's owner.

On tools and builders, Anthropic is previewing self hosted Claude Managed Agents, so customers can run the harness and sandboxes in their own cloud. It has also put Claude Meetings into beta for Team and Enterprise plans. Meta's Muse agent can now phone United States businesses for paying users, and plans start at twenty dollars a month. A caution from November tenth: security firm Claroc says share links from the Grok Build coding agent can be enumerated, exposing business data from thousands of apps.

In industry and policy, Nvidia's board said Huang left effective immediately, after reports of affairs including one with a woman accused of being a Chinese spy. Kress has been chief financial officer since twenty thirteen. House Foreign Affairs chairman Brian Mast said Huang agreed to testify behind closed doors by Thanksgiving. Representative Richard Neal and Senator Ron Wyden asked Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to preserve records on how chip licences for China were handled. As minority members, they cannot compel answers.

Anthropic's roadshow offers eight hundred twenty five million Class A shares at an expected seventy to seventy eight dollars each, and it has applied to list on Nasdaq as A N T. Nebius outlined forty billion dollars of spending for twenty twenty seven, funded by customer prepayments and contract backed loans. And the F A A says its eight hundred seventy five million dollar scheduling tool will now cover all twenty two air traffic centres. Those figures are the agency's own, and the controllers' union says it was not consulted.

Now the Playbook, four techniques from people who build these tools.

One. From Mihail Eric, who teaches at Stanford and leads A I at Monaco. Quiz yourself on the agent's patch before you accept it. Run an explain diff skill on the change, answer its questions without looking at the code, and spend your review time on the question that sent you back into the code.

Two. From Dominik Kundel and Charlie Guo, developer experience engineers at OpenAI. Use voice as a control plane. Use it to check in on threads, start new ones and hand work to the cloud, and turn the effort level down when a task is simple.

Three. From Boris Cherny of Claude Code. Do not commit the local settings file, use auto mode instead of hand kept allow and deny lists, and run a secret scanner, knowing that researchers found secrets two popular scanners missed.

Four. From October, Simon Willison. Name the library in your first prompt, say you want the result fun and beautiful, then follow up asking for a lot more fun.

Learn one thing. A mixture of experts model has several expert networks and a gating function that decides how much each contributes to an answer. That is why announcements quote two sizes. Total counts every expert. Active counts the part used at a time. Check which one a company is quoting.

The days ahead. Nvidia reports earnings on Tuesday, November seventeenth. Anthropic's offering is reportedly set to price on Wednesday, November eighteenth. Huang is due to testify by Thanksgiving, November twenty sixth. And on December first, Gemini Carbon and Argon prices reportedly double. That is The A I Dispatch.
